slides.title: Custom Allocators Overview
slides.prompt: Custom allocators handle memory allocation and deallocation strategies for STL containers. They allow developers to build specialized memory pools, arena allocators, or embedded system memory managers.

slides.title: Allocator allocate Method
slides.prompt: Fill in the required allocator method name that reserves uninitialized memory for n items.

slides.title: std::allocator_traits Purpose
slides.prompt: Why should container implementations use std::allocator_traits<Alloc> rather than calling allocator methods directly?
options: Provides backward compatibility and default implementations for optional allocator requirements
Enforces multithread locks around memory allocation calls
Automatically converts raw pointers to smart pointers
Optimizes runtime execution using SIMD instructions
slides.correctAnswer: Provides backward compatibility and default implementations for optional allocator requirements

slides.title: Deallocate Method
slides.prompt: Fill in the allocator method responsible for releasing memory block ptr.

slides.title: Memory Pool Benefit
slides.prompt: What primary performance bottleneck do memory pools address compared to global heap (new/malloc)?
options: Eliminates heap fragmentation and provides fast O(1) allocation time by pre-allocating contiguous chunks
slides.correctAnswer: Eliminates heap fragmentation and provides fast O(1) allocation time by pre-allocating contiguous chunks

slides.title: Constructing Object via Traits
slides.prompt: Fill in the traits function used to construct an object in pre-allocated memory.

slides.title: Stateful vs Stateless Allocator
slides.prompt: What defines a stateless allocator in C++?
options: All instances of the allocator type are equivalent and interchangeable (operator== always returns true)
It cannot allocate memory for classes with state member variables
It stores raw pointer references to a global arena pool
It works only with stack memory
slides.correctAnswer: All instances of the allocator type are equivalent and interchangeable (operator== always returns true)

slides.title: std::pmr (Polymorphic Memory Resource)
slides.prompt: What major feature did C++17 introduce in <memory_resource> via std::pmr?
options: Polymorphic allocators where container types don't change even when using different runtime memory resources
Automatic GPU memory allocation for vectors
slides.correctAnswer: Polymorphic allocators where container types don't change even when using different runtime memory resources
